# MirrorMire AMaze

Collect detection alerts, network security logs, and audit events from the
MirrorMire AMaze deception platform with Elastic Agent.

## Data streams

The AMaze integration collects three kinds of data:

| Data stream | Source API | Description |
|-------------|------------|-------------|
| `alerts` | `GET /api/v3/tickets` | Actionable incident tickets (detections) generated by AMaze |
| `logs` | `GET /api/v3/external/logs` | External-network SCA detection logs |
| `audit` | `GET /api/v3/audit-log` | Immutable audit trail of administrative actions |

Each data stream polls the AMaze REST API on a configurable interval, splits
the response into individual events, normalizes the fields into ECS, and
indexes them into Elasticsearch.

## Requirements

- Elastic Stack 8.x with Elastic Agent and Fleet.
- A MirrorMire AMaze deployment that exposes the REST API v3 (`/api/v3`).
- A bearer token (JWT or API token) with permission to read the resources
  above. Audit collection additionally requires an admin/auditor role.

## Setup

1. In Kibana, open **Integrations** and search for **AMaze**.
2. Click **Add AMaze**.
3. Configure the integration:

   | Setting | Description |
   |---------|-------------|
   | `Base URL` | Full AMaze API base URL including the API path, e.g. `https://dashboard.mirrormire.ai/api/v3`. |
   | `Bearer Token` | The JWT or API token used to authenticate against the AMaze API. |
   | `Verify TLS Certificates` | Set to `false` only for self-signed or on-prem instances. |
   | `Collection Interval` | How often to poll the AMaze API (default `5m`). |
   | `Initial Collection Interval` | Look-back window on the first poll (default `24h`). |

4. Save the policy and enroll an Elastic Agent.

## ECS mapping

Events are normalized to ECS. Original AMaze values are preserved in the
`amaze.*` namespace so no data is lost during transformation.

| AMaze field | ECS field |
|-------------|-----------|
| `id` | `event.id` |
| `src_ip` | `source.ip` |
| `dst_ip` | `destination.ip` |
| `protocol` | `network.protocol` |
| `threat_score` | `event.severity` |
| `ttp` | `threat.technique.id` |
| `title` | `event.action` |
| `created_at` / `timestamp` | `@timestamp` |
| `actor` | `user.email` |
| `action` | `event.action` |
| `country` | `source.geo.country_iso_code` |
| `username` | `source.user.name` |

All original values remain available under `amaze.*`, e.g.
`amaze.ticket_status`, `amaze.threat_score`, `amaze.ttp`, `amaze.src_ip`,
`amaze.dst_ip`, `amaze.title`, `amaze.actor`, `amaze.action`,
`amaze.country`, `amaze.username`.

## Troubleshooting

- **401 Unauthorized** — the bearer token is invalid or lacks the required
  role. Verify the token against `GET /api/v3/sites` with `curl`.
- **Self-signed TLS errors** — disable **Verify TLS Certificates**.
- **No documents arriving** — enable request tracing on the input
  (`request.tracer.enabled: true`) to inspect the raw HTTP exchange, then
  check the agent's logs.
- **Duplicate documents** — the `alerts` and `audit` data streams keep a
  cursor of the last seen timestamp so each poll only fetches new events.
  The `logs` stream is page-paginated; because the logs API has no
  timestamp filter, re-polling may return the same recent events.
